cases.name: caps-holding-a-window
cases.desc: A device that accepts UBX-MGA, keeps it across a power cycle, and is already holding orbit data valid to a stated instant.
cases.note: held_until uses the same type and units as gps_fix.t_utc, so a client comparing the two converts nothing.

cases.name: caps-holding-nothing
cases.desc: A device with no aiding loaded. held_until is zero AND its validity bit is clear; a client MUST conclude 'holds nothing', never 'valid until the Unix epoch'.
cases.note: validity, format and flags all differ from each other across this file's three caps vectors. Without that a decoder reading any one of the three from another's offset passes the whole corpus -- the hole mutation testing found in link_params' tx/rx pair.

cases.name: caps-without-persistence
cases.desc: A device holding a window that will not survive a power cycle. A client MUST NOT carry held_until forward to the next connection (SPEC.md 14.2).

cases.name: caps-stale-value-behind-cleared-bit
cases.desc: A non-conforming device that clears the held_until bit but leaves the previous window in the bytes. A decoder MUST report held_until absent on the strength of the bit alone.
cases.note: Not byte-canonical, so the round-trip also asserts that a conforming encoder normalises the field to zero. This is the only coverage the gnss_aid_caps encoder gate gets.

cases.name: caps-unknown-format
cases.desc: A format from a later minor version. A decoder MUST report it unknown, and a client MUST NOT open a transfer it cannot fill (SPEC.md 14.1).

cases.name: caps-reserved-flag-set
cases.desc: A later minor assigned aid_flags bit 4. A decoder MUST ignore the unknown bit and decode every known field normally, and a VTP/1.0 encoder MUST normalise it away on transmit (SPEC.md 2).

cases.name: caps-short-payload
cases.desc: 15 bytes. A truncated control response MUST be rejected whole.

cases.name: caps-long-payload
cases.desc: 17 bytes. gnss_aid_caps is fixed-size with no extension mechanism, so trailing bytes MUST be rejected.

cases.name: begin-at-full-mtu
cases.desc: A transfer opened at a 247-byte ATT MTU: 247 - 3 bytes of Write Command header - 3 bytes of chunk header (SPEC.md 14.3).
cases.note: chunk_bytes is fixed for the transfer because index-to-offset must be arithmetic; SPEC.md 14.3 gives the reason.

cases.name: begin-at-minimum-mtu
cases.desc: The same transfer at the 100-byte minimum ATT MTU this protocol requires. A device MUST NOT return a chunk_bytes a client cannot write.

cases.name: begin-short-payload
cases.desc: 3 bytes. A truncated begin result MUST be rejected whole.

cases.name: begin-long-payload
cases.desc: 5 bytes. aid_begin_result is fixed-size, so trailing bytes MUST be rejected.

cases.name: commit-applied
cases.desc: Every chunk arrived, the CRC matched, and the receiver took the data. The first_missing bit is clear, so a decoder MUST report the field absent rather than reading chunk 0 as missing.

cases.name: commit-incomplete
cases.desc: Chunks were lost on a write-without-response path. The client resends from index 113 and commits again; the transfer stays open (SPEC.md 14.4).

cases.name: commit-bad-crc
cases.desc: Every chunk arrived and the CRC-32 does not match. Nothing is missing, so there is no index to resend from and the transfer closes.

cases.name: commit-rejected
cases.desc: The transfer was intact and the receiver refused it -- the client sent well-formed bytes that this receiver will not take.

cases.name: commit-stale-index-behind-cleared-bit
cases.desc: A non-conforming device reporting `applied` while leaving the previous commit's missing index in the bytes. A decoder MUST report first_missing absent, and MUST NOT tell a user that chunk 113 was lost from a transfer that succeeded.
cases.note: The only coverage the aid_commit_result encoder gate gets.

cases.name: commit-unknown-result
cases.desc: A result from a later minor version. A decoder MUST report it unknown and MUST NOT coerce it to `applied` (SPEC.md 11.4).

cases.name: commit-short-payload
cases.desc: 3 bytes. A truncated commit result MUST be rejected whole.

cases.name: commit-long-payload
cases.desc: 5 bytes. aid_commit_result is fixed-size, so trailing bytes MUST be rejected.
